- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add slight upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price by 1–3% in 70%+ of cases when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — apply +1.5–2.5% adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00 values), model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual peak.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often misses the momentum; forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment turn.
